page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Use the sum-to-product identity
steps.margin_note: First mark. The identity sin C − sin D = 2 cos((C + D)/2) sin((C − D)/2) turns a difference of two sines into a product, and the half-sum here is simply a.
lines: At x = 0 the numerator is sin a − sin a = 0 and the denominator is 0, so the form is 0/0.
Use  sin C − sin D = 2 cos((C + D)/2) · sin((C − D)/2)  with C = a + bx and D = a − bx.
∴ sin(a + bx) − sin(a − bx) = 2 cos a · sin(bx)

recall.must_convey: That sin C − sin D = 2 cos((C+D)/2) sin((C−D)/2) is applied, giving 2 cos a · sin(bx).

steps.why: A difference of two sines cannot be cancelled against x as it stands. Turning it into a product isolates a single sin(bx), which is the only part that depends on x and the only part the standard limit is needed for.
common_mistakes: Expanding both sines with the compound-angle formula and then losing a term while subtracting.
Using the cos C − cos D identity, which carries a minus sign in front.
steps.memory_tip: For sin C − sin D the cosine takes the half-sum and the sine takes the half-difference. Here the half-sum is a, so cos a comes out as a constant.

steps.label: Apply lim sin θ / θ = 1
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Multiply and divide by b so the angle bx sits under its own sine. The b that comes out is where the factor b in the answer originates.
lines: lim(x → 0) (sin(a + bx) − sin(a − bx))/x = lim(x → 0) 2 cos a · sin(bx)/x
As x → 0, bx → 0, so lim(x → 0) sin(bx)/(bx) = 1.

lines.text: ∴ lim(x → 0) (sin(a + bx) − sin(a − bx))/x = 2b cos a

recall.must_convey: That sin(bx)/x is written as b · sin(bx)/(bx), the standard limit gives 1, and the answer is 2b cos a.

steps.why: sin θ/θ → 1 only when the same angle appears above and below, so the bx has to be created in the denominator. The value checks numerically: with a = 1 and b = 3 the answer is 6 cos 1 = 3.24181, and at x = 0.00001 the expression is 3.24181.
common_mistakes: Writing lim sin(bx)/x = 1 and losing the factor b.
Giving 2b sin a by swapping the cosine and the sine in the identity.
steps.memory_tip: sin(bx)/x is never 1; it is b. Whatever multiplies x inside the sine comes out in front.
